newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen confirms to work with Preussag on ships.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen confirms to work with Preussag on ships.

text.p: German industrial conglomerate Thyssen AG confirmed on Friday it plans to hold talks with Preussag AG on cooperating in shipbuilding.
Initial talks are planned for next week, with concrete negotiations due to start in autumn, but the results are open, a Thyssen spokesman said.
Thyssen confirms to work with Preussag on ships
The spokesman said no firm decisions had been made over future structures, or which company might have leadership in an eventual merger.
The subsidiaries involved are Thyssen's Blohm+Voss and Nordseewerke, and Preussag's Howaldtswerke.
The Hamburger Abendblatt daily reported on Friday the two companies would begin formal talks on cooperation in the next few weeks.
"The aim is an intensive form of cooperation, up to a change in the relations of ownership," the paper quoted Thyssen Industrie spokesman Alfred Wewers as saying.

It said Thyssen Industrie chairman Eckhard Rohkamm had not ruled out a merger. A merged company would be the biggest shipbuilder in Germany with 6,500 workers and a turnover of around 3.5 billion marks, the paper said.
Thyssen Industrie is the capital goods unit of Thyssen AG .
Blohm & Voss made heavy losses in 1995-96 but the Hamburger Abendblatt quoted the shipbuilder's works council chairman, Otto Tetau, as predicting a profit this year.
"Blohm & Voss will be in the black this year," he said. -- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750
